scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** OSPF route origination on `switch_dist_1_1` — the `network` statement covering the Pod 1 access subnet `10.1.1.0/24` is absent from its FRR OSPF configuration.

**Mechanism:** OSPF routers advertise only the prefixes explicitly covered by their `network` statements. `switch_dist_1_1` is only configured with `network 172.16.0.6/31 area 0.0.0.1`, which covers its uplink transit link to `router_core_1`. The access-side bridge interface `10.1.1.0/24` is never injected into OSPF area 0.0.0.1. As a result, no other router in the topology learns the 10.1.1.0/24 prefix — `router_core_1`'s RIB shows `10.2.1.0/24` and `10.200.0.0/24` but has no entry for `10.1.1.0/24`. When any external host or server tries to reach `10.1.1.2`, its gateway has no matching route and returns an ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable". Outbound traffic from `host_1_1_1_1` reaches `switch_dist_1_1` normally (gateway is on the local subnet), but core routers cannot forward return traffic, causing a one-way reachability break. `switch_dist_1_1` itself can reach the server farm because it *does* receive OSPF routes from peers — the missing advertisement only prevents others from routing *to* Pod 1.

**Localization:** `switch_dist_1_1`, FRR OSPF process, `network` statement for `10.1.1.0/24` in area `0.0.0.1`.

**Root cause:** `switch_dist_1_1` is missing `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1` in its OSPF configuration, so the Pod 1 access subnet is never advertised into the routing domain.

**Fix:** Add `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1` under `router ospf` in `switch_dist_1_1`'s FRR configuration (matching the symmetric configuration of its peer `switch_dist_2_1` which correctly includes `network 10.2.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1`).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names and localizes the fault to switch_dist_1_1 (OSPF network statement missing).

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies switch_dist_1_1 as missing the OSPF `network 10.1.1.0/24` statement and explains that 10.1.1.0/24 is not being advertised.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly describes the asymmetry: forward traffic reaches the pod but return traffic fails because the 10.1.1.0/24 prefix is not advertised, causing loss of the return route.

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)
per_axis.rationale: The writeup notes the switch has routes via its uplink but does not explicitly explain that its pings use the still-advertised uplink source address (172.16.0.7), as required.
Proposes adding the missing OSPF network statement for 10.1.1.0/24 on switch_dist_1_1 (area 1 / 0.0.0.1), which matches the expected remediation.
